column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: a registeredBackends test, so it runs one subtest per dialect and mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs (the cluster job runs ./engine/... too) while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by name rather than by delta, with CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL and CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset and CLEAT_TEST_POSTGRES set: go test ./engine/ -run TestTheReaperDoesNotReclaimASleepingWorkflow -count=1 -json reports exactly the mysql and mssql arms skipping and postgres passing. The arms have to exist even where they skip: cleat#1429 turns on the reaper predicate being status=running, and that predicate is written three times, once per dialect (store_lifecycle.go, mysql_lifecycle.go, mssql_operations.go), so a postgres-only run cannot vouch for the other two. Verified failable on postgres by widening the predicate to status IN (running, ready): reclaim_count goes asleep=1 and the test reddens -- while BOTH rows still read status=ready, which is why the assertion is on reclaim_count and not on status.
